airport: large aviation area with visible runways, terminal-like facilities, and broad paved zones.
bareland: broad exposed ground with barren surface and little vegetation.
baseballfield: compact sports field with a clear baseball-diamond layout and central infield geometry.
beach: bright shoreline area with clear sand-water boundary and elongated coastal texture.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land.
center: dense urban core with concentrated buildings and organized city-block structure.
church: prominent religious building or complex with distinctive central architecture and surrounding open space.
commercial: organized business district with dense building blocks, roads, and urban infrastructure.
denseresidential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal open spacing.
desert: wide sandy or arid region with homogeneous barren texture and very little vegetation.
farmland: regular cultivated land with organized field parcels and crop texture.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture and little visible built structure.
industrial: large factory-like compounds with utilitarian building layouts, storage yards, and production infrastructure.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries.
mediumresidential: moderately spaced residential buildings with visible streets and yards.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with strong relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic structure.
park: planned green open space with vegetation, paths, and leisure-oriented spatial organization.
parking: large open paved area with organized parking spaces and vehicle-oriented rows.
playground: recreational activity area with sports or play surfaces and open activity layout.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact water shape and visible boundary.
port: waterfront transport area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent logistics structure.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures.
resort: leisure-oriented built environment with organized open spaces and accommodation-like structures.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks.
school: campus-like area with multiple institutional buildings, open grounds, and organized academic layout.
sparseresidential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density.
square: open civic plaza-like space embedded in an urban area.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field or arena and surrounding spectator-related structure.
storagetanks: clusters of large circular storage tanks with highly regular round geometry.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with clear grade-separated roadway form.
